factual_methodology.summary: UK September CPI and CPIH, producer indices, and fiscal stock/flow distinctions checked against 21 October ONS releases; policy and forecast vintages explicitly separated.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: UK energy inflation, fiscal stress, banking policy and international transmission distinct from prior day's US housing theme.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Parallel two charts, tables, flow and regional map; numerical chart series verified identical EN/PT.

research_depth.summary: Multiple analytical sections, distributional analysis, three conditional scenarios and observable disconfirming evidence.

evidence_traceability.summary: Eight same institutional URLs for ONS, BoE, EIA, IMF, Eurostat and Fed with dated figures and conceptual limitations.

counterfactual_review.summary: Differentiates one-time relative energy price shock, persistent underlying inflation and fiscal amplification; contrary evidence includes declining UK debt-to-GDP ratio.

contrary_evidence: UK debt-to-GDP ratio was lower year on year despite nominal debt passing £3 trillion.
Year-to-date UK borrowing was below the prior-year period even though the September reading was higher and cumulative borrowing exceeded forecast.
UK consumer transport inflation had a large fuel component, but the data cannot attribute all core services price movements directly to oil.
limitations: Headline CPI/CPIH, factory producer prices, UK public finances and international industrial output have differing units, coverage and reference periods.
October IMF/EIA forecasts were completed using information principally through 1 October, prior to the UK data released 21 October.
No live October 21 closing market yields or implied policy probabilities were asserted; this is internal editorial review, not external peer review.
notes: Internal editorial and bilingual parity review using contemporaneous primary institutional releases. Numerical figures, calendar vintages and nonadditivity caveats checked; scenario statements are conditional.

en.title: Global Macro — British inflation accelerates while energy costs and debt financing test policy resilience
en.deck: The UK reports 3.5% annual CPI inflation, 8.3% producer input inflation and £24.52 billion in monthly borrowing, exposing the transmission of energy shocks into prices and public finances.
en.regime: Energy-driven inflation acceleration, heterogeneous industrial activity and persistent interest-rate/fiscal constraints.
en.key_risk: Energy shocks become persistent core and service inflation while indexed debt costs narrow fiscal policy space.

producer_checks.visual_signature: Two separate quantitative charts, two substantive tables, causal flow and comparative regional map per language.
producer_checks.source_check: Eight identical institutional source URLs: ONS CPI, ONS PPI, ONS fiscal series, Bank of England, EIA, IMF, Eurostat and Federal Reserve. Original release dates and frequencies differentiated.
